Review of Dr. Woraphot's Dental Clinic (Treatment with Dr. Beam)

I recently had my lower wisdom tooth extracted and my upper wisdom tooth removed by Dr. Beam today. I must say, I was very impressed. From the moment I walked in until the procedure was complete, it was an unexpectedly positive wisdom tooth extraction experience.

Dr. Beam explained every step in detail, clearly, and in an easy-to-understand way, from reviewing the X-rays and analyzing the wisdom tooth's position to the various risks involved (I am 33 years old and have diabetes, and the doctor gave very careful advice).

Before the surgery, the doctor checked my blood pressure, explained everything calmly, and told me exactly what he was going to do next, which made me feel very comfortable and not anxious at all.

He injected the anesthetic twice to ensure complete numbness. The first injection was enough, but the doctor was so attentive that he even wanted my lips to be numb for added comfort during the surgery.

Once the surgery began… I must say, the doctor's touch was incredibly gentle.
My lower wisdom tooth was also "lying" (intermittently), but it took less than 10 minutes.
Afterward, the doctor asked if I wanted to have it extracted completely, which I agreed to. The upper wisdom tooth took less than a minute to complete.

The doctor spoke to me throughout the procedure.
“You’ll hear a loud sound here.”
“You’ll feel a slight push here.”
“Just a little more. Excellent!”

The feeling was great. It was like the doctor was perfectly timed and meticulous.

After the procedure, Dr. Beam gave a very detailed post-operative instruction summary.

He also provided gauze, medication, and scheduled an appointment for suture removal.

Regarding the price, I think it was very fair.

X-ray: 500 baht

Lower wisdom tooth extraction + upper wisdom tooth extraction: 3,700 baht (including suture removal)

Medication cost: 40 baht

Overall, it was very worthwhile considering the meticulous work and care received.

For anyone who is afraid of dentists, afraid of pain, or has had bad wisdom tooth extractions before,
I highly recommend Dr. Beam.
He’s gentle, kind, explains things well, works quickly, does a great job, and is very safe.

⭐ I left feeling, “I’m so glad I came here.”
Truly impressed! 🙏💚

I went to get dentures, asking for the pink base type I usually wear, but the dentist recommended the type with a metal frame to hold the teeth together.
- The procedure was in early October 2015.
- A week later, my dentures cracked on the upper, white side of my teeth, but the pink base remained intact. I went back to the dentist and they fixed it for free the first time, but they said there would be a fee for the next one. *I'm not sure if the white on my upper teeth is very thin, which might have caused the cracks.
- A month and 10 days later, both the upper and lower white and pink dentures cracked.
#I eat normally, but I don't bite anything very hard. I don't know if eating fried bananas is considered hard, because today they cracked. I don't eat fried foods that are that hard because they press on my gums and cause pain.
- I used to have dentures with pink bases for 5 years without cracking, but I forgot them when I went on a trip upcountry and had them done there, so I didn't go to the same dentist.
#I might be better suited to a non-metal base. This is something to consider when choosing a denture provider.

I'm someone who's terrified of dentists. This was my second visit, and I was impressed both times. The first time, I saw an older dentist who did a scaling; he was very gentle. The second time, I saw a younger dentist who needed a tooth extracted. I told him I was afraid of dentists, and he calmed me down by talking to me and giving me advice on what else needed to be done and how many teeth needed extraction. The second dentist was incredibly gentle. Before I could even get over my fear, he said, "The tooth is out!" He probably only wiggled it about seven times. I was shocked because I had a previous extraction elsewhere that left my jaw locked for days. I initially thought I would cry like the last time, but this time I left the dental room laughing, finding it funny that I was so scared.

Today I went to the doctor for gingivitis.
The doctor diagnosed it as tartar buildup causing swollen gums and pus. He recommended getting a tartar removal after my braces are removed and just gave me medication. That's it!!! But I went because it was swollen and painful, making it impossible to eat. I asked if the pus could be removed (my understanding, as someone who isn't a doctor, was that pus wouldn't just go away with medication; I thought it should be removed). I'd been to another clinic before where the doctor examined me, said it was due to food particles, then injected local anesthetic, drained the pus, cleaned my tooth, and gave me mouthwash and oral medication. It cleared up in 1-2 days.

After asking if the pus could be removed, the doctor here said yes. They removed the pus using a special instrument, pressing it out of the gum without any anesthetic. They pressed very hard and repeatedly; it was incredibly painful and agonizing. I cried uncontrollably on the operating table with my mouth open. It was embarrassing, but I couldn't hold back. I just burst into tears. Even without gingivitis, I would have felt pain, but this was the most excruciating pain I've ever experienced in my life – the kind of pain that makes you unable to eat.
